categories.title: Voice
categories.question: Do you have a voice service for the narration?

tools.name: ElevenLabs
tools.what_you_get: A natural human-sounding narration voice instead of the free built-in voice (basic quality, this computer's own speech engine).
tools.example: A natural voice for a 15 minute episode: the kit voices the script in chunks, pays for each chunk once, and checks your character allowance first.
connect: Make an ElevenLabs account at elevenlabs.io (check the site for what the plans include).
Open the key page in your account and create an API key.
Save it in the file ~/.config/bagelunit-reels/elevenlabs.key (the Reel Kit setup makes the empty file; paste the key yourself, never into the chat).
Run video doctor: it should say the key file exists.

tools.name: Another voice service
tools.what_you_get: Any other text-to-speech or recorded narration you already use.
tools.example: Your own recording of the script, or a voice from another service, dropped in as the episode's audio.
connect: Tell Claude which service you use; the kit does not require a particular one.
Keep the key or login with you: it is never asked for, printed or stored by the kit.

categories.title: Music and sound effects
categories.question: Do you have a library for music or sound effects?

tools.name: Uppbeat
tools.what_you_get: Licensed music (and some effects) you can use in a monetised YouTube video, recorded in the channel's licensed register with its licence.
tools.example: A different music bed per chapter, ducked under the voice, recorded with its licence so the credits and the upload check are done for you.
connect: Make an Uppbeat account and pick a plan that covers your use (check the site).
Download a track by hand and safelist your channel in your Uppbeat account.
Record it with video licensed add <file> --type music --title ... --source uppbeat --plan ...; the kit never downloads anything for you.

tools.name: Epidemic Sound
tools.what_you_get: A large licensed music and sound effect catalogue, searchable from Claude when its connector is on.
tools.example: Ask for a tense low strings bed for the investigation chapter and a door slam for the cold open, download them yourself and record them with their licence.
connect: Make an Epidemic Sound account and plan that covers YouTube (check the site).
Optional: turn on the Epidemic Sound connector in your Claude account (Connectors) so Claude can search it.
Download each file by hand and record it with video licensed add (--source epidemic-sound).

categories.title: 3D
categories.question: Do you have Blender for 3D shots?

tools.name: Blender (with the Blender Lab MCP)
tools.what_you_get: Free 3D rendering for hero objects, titles and maps; the Blender Lab MCP lets Claude work in a live Blender window.
tools.example: A shaded-relief map of the mountain range for a geography episode, or a 3D hero object for a cold open, rendered into the video's assets/blender/ folder.
connect: Install Blender 4.2 or newer from blender.org (free). The installer prints the one command for your system.
Run video doctor: it should say Blender was found.
Optional: install the official Blender Lab MCP so Claude can work live; claude mcp list then shows a blender server.
Use /blender-shot for the first shot.

categories.title: Generated video
categories.question: Do you have a generated-video tool?

tools.name: Higgsfield
tools.what_you_get: Short generated video shots from a prompt or a still, for moments no footage exists of. Generated shots must be labelled as re-creations.
tools.example: A 5 second establishing shot of a 1900s factory floor between chapters, labelled Re-creation, brought in as your own clip.
connect: Make a Higgsfield account (check the site for what the plans include).
Optional: turn on the Higgsfield connector in your Claude account so Claude can generate shots for you.
Save each shot you keep inside the channel folder and use it as a "file" clip.

tools.name: Another generated-video tool
tools.what_you_get: Any other tool that makes short clips from a prompt.
tools.example: A short clip you generated elsewhere, saved into the channel folder and used as a clip between two chapters.
connect: Tell Claude which tool you use; any clip saved in the channel folder works as a "file" clip.
Label generated shots as re-creations on screen.

categories.title: Design
categories.question: Do you have a design tool for thumbnails and graphics?

tools.name: Canva
tools.what_you_get: Designed thumbnails and graphics from your own templates, with Claude working through the Canva connector.
tools.example: A thumbnail from your channel template in two minutes, then video thumbnail --image to add the kit's text treatment and size it to 1280x720.
connect: Make a Canva account (check the site for what the plans include).
Optional: turn on the Canva connector in your Claude account so Claude can open and export designs.
Export the design as an image into the channel folder and run video thumbnail --image <file>.

tools.name: Adobe Firefly or Adobe Express
tools.what_you_get: Generated and designed images, backgrounds and thumbnails in Adobe's web tools.
tools.example: A moody background for a thumbnail generated in Firefly, then used with video thumbnail --image and your headline.
connect: Sign in at firefly.adobe.com or express.adobe.com (check the site for what your plan includes).
Save the image into the channel folder and run video thumbnail --image <file>.

tools.name: Adobe connector for Claude
tools.what_you_get: Lets Claude work with your Adobe tools directly instead of you moving files by hand.
tools.example: Claude opens your Express template, swaps the headline and exports the image for video thumbnail --image.
connect: Turn on the Adobe connector in your Claude account (Connectors), if your account offers it.
Sign in to Adobe when asked.

categories.title: Research and competitors
categories.question: Do you have a research or scraping tool?

tools.name: Apify
tools.what_you_get: A pay-as-you-go scraping platform. Saved once as a token, it lets the kit read other YouTube channels' public video lists (titles, views, publish dates) so you can track competitors and see which topics work for them. The Reel Kit already uses the same token to read Instagram accounts; a YouTube competitor tracker for this kit builds on it.
tools.example: the last 30 videos of five rival channels: which ones beat that channel's own median views, and what their titles and thumbnails have in common, to feed your next outline
connect: Make an Apify account and check the site for the current plan, free credit and usage terms.
Create an API token at console.apify.com/settings/integrations (Claude can open the page with the browser tool; you copy the token yourself).
Save it alone on one line in ~/.config/bagelunit-reels/apify.key (the same file the Reel Kit uses; Claude makes the empty file and opens it for you; never paste the token into the chat).
Reading other channels costs money on Apify's side: the kit shows the estimated cost first and runs nothing without your yes.
